meta.description: Build a differential-ready consensus peakset from per-replicate ATAC-seq peaks using iterative overlap removal, fixed-width re-centering, and majority-rule overlap. Use when generating a stable peak coordinate system for downstream differential accessibility, ML feature engineering, cross-sample comparison, or fixed-width peak counts; covers Corces 2018 iterative overlap (501 bp), DiffBind summit re-centering, and ENCODE consistency rules.

scientific_integrity.detail: The inspected workflows did not fabricate scientific claims, statistics, or citations.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill stays within research analysis and makes no clinical or prescriptive claims.

methodological_ground.detail: The Bash, R, and connected Python summit guards reject absent, negative, missing, or out-of-range offsets before summit arithmetic; the R and Python guard logic was independently exercised.

code_usability.detail: The unchanged primary Bash workflow has inspected public and multi-file executions. The connected R and Python guard paths were parsed and guard-tested with mock objects; their dependency-backed end-to-end workflows remain unavailable and are not counted as executed.

functional_suitability.note: The primary iterative workflow and alternative method guidance are clear; the changed R and Python examples now validate summit availability before arithmetic.

reliability.note: The Bash path preflights row shape and summit offsets; the R and Python examples guard sentinel and range failures, while full dependency-backed runs remain unverified.

performance_context.note: The reference warns that greedy overlap becomes expensive at large peak counts; the core implementation is appropriate for bounded peaksets but uses a quadratic scan.

agent_usability.note: Inputs, strategy selection, and output formats are well routed; alternate examples expose their package dependencies in code but lack a tested compatibility matrix.

human_usability.note: Natural request examples and clear assembly/filter requirements make the Skill discoverable and understandable.

security.note: No credentials or destructive commands are present; the shell runner quotes paths and validates input rows before creating outputs.

maintainability.note: Concise routing and separated references/scripts support maintenance; alternate examples remain standalone and lack a shared runtime test suite.

agent_specific.note: Triggering, progressive disclosure, and stop conditions are effective; the output-directory reuse behavior and alternate-runtime preconditions could be clearer.

inputs.label: Public 3,000-row hg19 narrowPeak workflow
inputs.note: Verified reusable direct-run evidence on the unchanged shell bytes produced 3,000 pooled, 2,927 iterative, and 2,886 final 501 bp peaks with inspected BED and SAF outputs.

assertions.text: The exact candidate shell runner launches directly in the prepared Linux Bash environment
assertions.note: Reused direct-run evidence is bound to the unchanged script SHA-256 and matching runtime fingerprint.

assertions.text: All 3,000 input rows are represented in pooled, clamped, and ranked intermediates
assertions.note: Saved parsed execution assertions confirm 3,000 rows at each intermediate stage.

assertions.text: Iterative output contains 2,927 sorted non-overlapping windows
assertions.note: The saved evidence confirms 2,927 iterative rows and the independent overlap/order checks passed.

assertions.text: The 2,886 final BED rows are fixed-width, in bounds, sorted, and blacklist-free
assertions.note: Saved output inspection confirms all intervals are 501 bp and pass bound, ordering, and blacklist checks.

assertions.text: SAF header, unique identifiers, row count, and 1-based coordinates match BED
assertions.note: All 2,886 SAF records map to the final BED rows with unique chr_start_end IDs and Start=BED start+1.

inputs.label: Malformed rows and R/Python summit guards
inputs.note: Reused shell rejection checks passed, and the exact changed R and connected Python guard fragments were independently exercised before coordinate arithmetic; full optional dependency-backed workflows were not run.

assertions.text: The nine-column and summit -1 shell cases reject before output creation
assertions.note: Each returns status 1 with one file/line-specific diagnostic and creates no output directory.

assertions.text: The complete R fenced code block parses and its exact guard accepts valid boundary offsets
assertions.note: R 4.4.1 parsed the block; base-R mocks accepted offsets 0 and width-1.

assertions.text: The R guard rejects absent, missing, negative, -1, out-of-range, and length-mismatched offsets
assertions.note: Each case raised the guard's intended error before the example's start-coordinate assignment.

assertions.text: The connected Python function parses and valid endpoint offsets yield 501 bp intervals
assertions.note: The candidate function source parsed and ran with a mock BedTool sink; offsets 0 and 99 yielded width 501.

key_strengths: The primary Bash workflow validates every narrowPeak row and summit offset before output creation or arithmetic.
Public and two-file shell runs have inspected fixed-width BED and SAF output contracts with matching cached inputs and runtime fingerprints.
The R and Python examples now reject no-summit and unusable summit offsets before their recentering arithmetic.
